daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

A significant controversy has erupted over a proposal by senior minister Luhut Pandjaitan to remove state financial loss as a defining element of corruption, with Justice Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra stating the current definition makes SOE officials afraid to make decisions. The proposal has drawn swift opposition, with ICW rejecting the idea, saying it would make Indonesia appear clean from corruption, while the Law Minister clarified the proposal remains only a concept. The debate marks a potential shift in Indonesia's anti-corruption framework that has faced widespread rejection.

  • President Prabowo marked his two-year anniversary by calling his government's performance impressive and stating he follows Joko Widodo's political line.
  • The KPK revealed that two active TNI soldiers are involved in an alleged corruption case at the national disaster agency BNPB.
  • Maritime Affairs Minister Nusron Wahid attended a cabinet meeting at the palace after failing to respond to two KPK summonses, having traveled to Singapore when he was scheduled to be questioned.
  • PDIP rejected accusations from Jokowi regarding alleged political operations behind the diploma controversy.
  • A Constitutional Court hearing saw judges sharply questioning petitioners challenging the Election Law who claimed O-Level graduates can attend university.
  • The Presidential Advisory Council defended itself after being sued at the Constitutional Court for allegedly burdening the state budget.
  • The Law Minister opened the possibility of regulating ecological terrorism in legislation.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and the United States have launched a collaboration to protect the historic wreck of the USS Houston, with the Maritime Affairs Ministry involving local communities in safeguarding the underwater heritage site. The initiative represents a bilateral effort to preserve Indonesia's underwater cultural heritage through U.S. support programs.

  • President Prabowo emphasized that Indonesia is stepping up defense modernization under his leadership.
  • UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese urged Indonesia to evaluate economic ties with what she termed genocide in Gaza.
  • Indonesia and Malaysia are pushing joint film and music production to deepen cultural ties between the two nations.
  • The Special Rapporteur stated that Indonesia can lead the formation of multilateralism at the United Nations.

Other

Indonesia is racing to protect its emerging market status against potential downgrade by MSCI, with President Prabowo defiantly declaring Indonesia is not afraid of anyone and will not be intimidated by the pressure. The Coordinating Minister for the Economy downplayed concerns, calling MSCI ripples that are not disturbing, while Indonesia has pledged tangible capital market reforms to boost investor confidence.

  • Energy Minister Bahlil announced plans to halt gas exports to other countries, stating Indonesia is in "survival mode," while Prabowo separately emphasized a domestic energy push and warned against foreign interference in Indonesia's natural wealth.
  • Authorities have named 11 corporations as suspects in forest fire cases, amid Prabowo's warning to nations insulting Indonesia over the fires and Polkam denials of conflict of interest in handling the cases.
  • Danantara and BP BUMN plan to leverage state assets to develop 12 smart cities across Indonesia.
  • Indonesia's forex hedging incentives have attracted $9.9 billion in foreign capital inflows.
  • Two ministers confirmed that civil servant salaries will not flow through village cooperatives, with the Cooperatives Minister speaking out on the matter.
